long_biography.plain_text:
Towson Mechanical traces its regional operations to 1962, building a portfolio around the difficult coordination demands of schools, secure correctional facilities and other large public buildings. Its present federal registration describes an active commercial and institutional building contractor, with Shawn Raver serving as its government-business principal.

A completed renovation at Baltimore/Washington International Airport illustrates the firm's project work. The assignment replaced ceiling and lighting systems across two concourses, where Maryland's architectural awards record names Raver in Towson Mechanical's general-contractor team. The finished scheme integrated an unconventional geometric ceiling with new lighting across more than 26,000 square feet of terminal space.
